headline: Runner Guilds Step Into the Light: Contractor Pools Now Accepting Corporate Registrations
body:
Something shifted this week that six months ago would have sounded like a bad joke: Meridian 88's three largest runner collective networks — the Ironshed Pool, Faultline Associates, and the still-technically-anonymous group operating under the handle Deadweight — have all filed limited liability registrations with the Federal Remnant's Commercial Contractors Bureau. The filings do not use the word 'runner.' They describe themselves as 'contingency logistics and asset facilitation services,' which is the most expensive-sounding way anyone has ever said 'we move things and people for money.' Tessera and Palladian are named in the filings as inaugural registered clients. The Federal Remnant approved all three registrations within 72 hours — a processing speed that normally takes six weeks and suggests someone upstairs wanted this to happen.

The semi-legitimization push has been building since the 2194 Meridian Security Compact, a Federal Remnant framework that quietly allowed corponations to contract 'unlicensed asset facilitators' for operations in disputed or ungoverned zones — meaning Old Harbor, deep Narrows corridors, and the Underworld — without direct liability exposure. What was a legal gray corridor has apparently widened into something resembling a front door. Iron Lotus is reportedly furious, and not only for ideological reasons: the syndicate has run informal runner placement for years and now faces legitimate competition for contract origination. 'They put a tax ID on the underground and called it progress,' said one runner who asked not to be named, speaking from a location in The Shelf. 'I'm not sure if I'm supposed to be relieved or insulted.'

The practical effects are already visible in The Circuit's contract markets. Registered runner pools can now access corponation escrow systems for payment — meaning 14,000 quanta jobs that previously required handshake trust and sometimes violence to collect are now enforceable through commercial arbitration. That is unambiguously good for runners who were getting robbed by clients. It is also, critics note, good for corponations who now have documented leverage over operatives who were previously untouchable. The Graycloaks published an analysis overnight suggesting that registration creates a paper trail that the Federal Remnant's intelligence division — and by extension, anyone who can buy Federal data — can follow.

The Wishing Well movement released a characteristically oblique statement calling the registrations 'the city learning to name what it already knew it needed.' The Bore Rats have not commented. Deep Underworld runner networks with no interest in legitimacy are understood to be watching the registered pools with something between contempt and careful attention.
aftermath: By 2198, eleven runner collectives had filed Federal registrations, and the Ironshed Pool had signed a standing logistics contract with Ferrogate Transit — a deal that made it the first runner organization in Meridian history to appear on a corponation's official vendor list.
runner_relevance: This event is the runner economy meta-story: semi-legitimization split the contractor market into two distinct tiers with different risk profiles and different clients. Registered runners gained access to escrow-backed corporate contracts — protection details, courier runs through disputed zones, licensed extraction work — but surrendered anonymity and created legal exposure. Unregistered runners found their informal contract networks disrupted as Iron Lotus tightened its grip on the remaining gray-market placement infrastructure to compensate for lost volume. The immediate contract boom was in transition facilitation — runners with existing reputations were hired by the new registered pools to quietly vouch for or vet other operatives, and several Graycloaks contracts went out specifically to identify which registered runners were also feeding intelligence back to the Federal Remnant's security division.
